claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has previously been produced in a hierarchical-heterostructured state with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A hybrid ML framework using reduced-order simulation descriptors can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Reduced-order descriptors can capture the relevant hierarchical microstructural and chemical fluctuations in HfNbTiVAl10.
Misfit volumes and elastic properties are physically relevant inputs for predicting alloy strengthening.
Surface energies and unstable stacking-fault energies are physically relevant inputs for models of alloy ductility.
Grain-boundary distributions, phase connectivity, and spatial chemical fluctuations influence local elastic and plastic responses.
An ML model can learn nonlinear relationships between reduced-order microstructural descriptors and macroscopic stiffness, yielding, and fracture toughness.
The proposed framework can make rapid predictions without running full-scale CALPHAD or first-principles calculations for every prediction.
The framework could predict Young's modulus and yield strength with errors below approximately 5–10% relative to experiment.
The framework could predict fracture toughness with errors below approximately 5–10% relative to experiment.
The framework could provide a computational speedup greater than tenfold relative to traditional high-fidelity simulations.
Ab initio and molecular-dynamics calculations are too time-consuming for routine high-throughput alloy-structure prediction.
CALPHAD calculations can require significant computing resources and can be limited by inadequate HEA databases.
Conventional ML performance depends on the size and composition of its training dataset.
Direct prediction of fracture and yield behavior is largely beyond available DFT implementations.
The framework's reliability depends on the representativeness of its training data.
The framework's reliability depends on the fidelity of its reduced-order descriptors.
Predictions may become unreliable for extreme chemical fluctuations, novel microstructures, high temperatures, or very high strain rates outside the calibration range.
